title: Create a two-rate income tax of 15% and 30%
proposal: Treasury should work with Congress on a simple two-bracket income tax of 15 and 30 percent that removes most deductions, credits, and exclusions, with the 30 percent rate starting near the Social Security wage base.
quote: enacting a simple two-rate individual tax system of 15 percent and 30 percent that eliminates most deductions, credits and exclusions.

title: Cut the corporate income tax rate to 18%
proposal: The corporate income tax rate should be lowered to 18 percent.
quote: The corporate income tax rate should be reduced to 18 percent.

title: Tax capital gains and dividends at 15%
proposal: Capital gains and qualified dividends should be taxed at 15 percent.
quote: Capital gains and qualified dividends should be taxed at 15 percent.

title: Allow full expensing and inflation-indexed capital gains
proposal: The tax system should let businesses immediately deduct capital investments and adjust capital gains for inflation.
quote: The system should allow immediate expensing for capital expenditures and index capital gains taxes for inflation.

title: Repeal Inflation Reduction Act tax increases
proposal: All tax increases in the Inflation Reduction Act should be repealed, including the book minimum tax, stock buyback tax, coal and Superfund taxes, and drug manufacturer excise taxes.
quote: intermediate tax reform should repeal all tax increases that were passed as part of the Inflation Reduction Act,

title: Repeal green energy tax credits
proposal: The administration should push to fully repeal recent tax subsidies, including the green energy credits and tax breaks in the Inflation Reduction Act.
quote: push for legislation to fully repeal recently passed subsidies in the tax code, including the dozens of credits and tax breaks for green energy companies

title: Create Universal Savings Accounts
proposal: All taxpayers should be able to put up to $15,000 a year of after-tax income into flexible Universal Savings Accounts with tax-free growth and withdrawals.
quote: All taxpayers should be allowed to contribute up to $15,000 (adjusted for inflation) of post-tax earnings into Universal Savings Accounts (USAs).

title: Expand business loss deductions
proposal: The business loss limit should rise to at least $500,000, and businesses should be able to fully carry forward net operating losses.
quote: Businesses should also be allowed to fully carry forward net operating losses.

title: Eliminate the net investment income tax and BEAT
proposal: The net investment income surtax and the base erosion anti-abuse tax should be eliminated.
quote: The net investment income surtax and the base erosion anti-abuse tax should be eliminated.

title: Lower the estate tax and make the higher exemption permanent
proposal: The estate and gift tax rate should be cut to no more than 20 percent, and the 2017 law's higher exemption should be made permanent.
quote: The estate and gift tax should be reduced to no higher than 20 percent,

title: Lower the tax on global intangible income (GILTI)
proposal: The tax on global intangible low-taxed income should be cut to no more than 12.5 percent, with limits on related foreign tax credits reduced or removed.
quote: The tax on global intangible low-taxed income should be reduced to no higher than 12.5 percent,

title: Permanently repeal deductions suspended in 2017
proposal: Non-business deductions suspended by the 2017 tax law, such as moving expenses and miscellaneous itemized deductions, should be permanently repealed.
quote: should be permanently repealed, including the bicycle commuting expense exclusion, non-military moving expense deductions, and the miscellaneous itemized deductions.

title: Fully repeal the state and local tax (SALT) deduction
proposal: The deduction for state and local taxes, now capped at $10,000, should be fully repealed.
quote: The individual state and local tax deduction, which was temporarily capped at $10,000, should be fully repealed.

title: Repeal tax deductions for education expenses
proposal: Tax deductions related to educational expenses should be repealed.
quote: Deductions related to educational expenses should be repealed.

title: Eliminate special business tax breaks
proposal: Special business tax preferences, such as the deduction for energy-efficient commercial buildings, should be eliminated.
quote: such as a special deduction for energy-efficient commercial building properties, should be eliminated.

title: Cap tax-free employee benefits at $12,000
proposal: Employers' deductions for untaxed employee benefits, other than retirement contributions, should be capped at no more than $12,000 per full-time worker per year, not indexed to inflation.
quote: set a meaningful cap (no higher than $12,000 per year per full-time equivalent employee—and preferably lower) on untaxed benefits that employers can claim as deductions.

title: End tax deductions for benefits to dependents 23 and older
proposal: Employers should not be able to deduct health insurance and other benefits for employees' dependents aged 23 or older.
quote: Employers should also be denied deductions for health insurance and other benefits provided to employee dependents if the dependents are aged 23 or older.

title: Move to a consumption-based tax system
proposal: After intermediate changes, the administration should pursue fundamental reform toward a consumption tax, such as a national sales tax, business transfer tax, flat tax, or cash flow tax.
quote: There are several forms that a consumption tax could take, including a national sales tax, a business transfer tax, a Hall–Rabushka flat tax

title: Require a three-fifths vote to raise tax rates
proposal: Treasury should support a law requiring a three-fifths vote in the House and Senate to raise income or corporate tax rates.
quote: Treasury should support legislation instituting a three-fifths vote threshold in the U.S. House and the Senate to raise income or corporate tax rates

title: Reject the global minimum corporate tax
proposal: The U.S. should not join a global minimum corporate tax or let international organizations set its tax policy.
quote: The U.S. should not outsource its tax policy to international organizations.

title: Withdraw from the OECD
proposal: The U.S. should stop funding the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development and withdraw from it.
quote: The United States provides about one-fifth of OECD’s funding.33 The U.S. should end its

title: Reverse the $80 billion IRS funding increase
proposal: The chapter says Congress should reverse the Inflation Reduction Act's roughly $80 billion expansion of the IRS.
quote: Unless Congress reverses this policy, the IRS will become much more intrusive and impose still greater costs on the American people.

title: Oppose $600 bank account reporting to the IRS
proposal: The chapter says a proposed rule requiring banks to report on accounts with more than $600 should be firmly opposed.
quote: it has proposed creating a comprehensive financial account information reporting regime that would apply to all business and personal accounts with more than $600.

title: Make more IRS leaders presidential appointees
proposal: Congress should make several top IRS officials, including deputy commissioners, division heads, and the National Taxpayer Advocate, presidential appointees.
quote: Congress should ensure that the Deputy Commissioner for Services and Enforcement, the Deputy Commissioner for Operations Support, the National Taxpayer Advocate,

title: Replace IRS technology leadership and review IT contracts
proposal: A Deputy Commissioner with strong IT skills should be appointed, subordinates replaced, IT contracts reviewed, and the modernization plan carried out cost-effectively.
quote: Deputy Commissioner should be replaced. A thorough review of IT contracts should be conducted.

title: Create a private-sector IT oversight board for the IRS
proposal: An oversight board of private-sector IT experts should be created with authority to oversee IRS technology work.
quote: composed of private sector IT experts should be established and given the authority to conduct meaningful, contemporaneous oversight.

title: Equal interest rates on tax overpayments and underpayments
proposal: Congress should make the interest the IRS pays on overpayments the same as the interest taxpayers pay on underpayments.
quote: interest on overpayments should be the same as interest on underpayments rather than the government receiving a higher rate,

title: Give taxpayers more time to sue over improper IRS collection
proposal: Congress should extend the time limit for taxpayers to sue for damages over improper IRS collection actions.
quote: the time limit for taxpayers to sue for damages for improper collection actions should be extended,

title: Expand Tax Court jurisdiction
proposal: Congress should expand the types of cases the Tax Court can hear.
quote: of the Tax Court should be expanded, and the tax penalty system should be

title: Reform and reduce IRS penalties
proposal: Congress should reform the tax penalty system by simplifying its structure and reducing some of the harshest penalties.
quote: the tax penalty system should be reformed by rationalizing the penalty structure and reducing some of the most punitive penalties.

title: Increase funding for the Taxpayer Advocate
proposal: Congress should give the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate more resources, at least 20 percent more (about $44 million).
quote: Congress should provide the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate with greater resources so that it may better assist taxpayers suffering from wrongful IRS actions.

title: Strengthen the Taxpayer Advocate's independence
proposal: The National Taxpayer Advocate should control its own staffing, get access to IRS information, be included in rulemaking, and be allowed to file court briefs independently.
quote: Ensuring that the National Taxpayer Advocate can make his or her own personnel decisions to protect its independence;

title: Reduce tax information reporting burdens
proposal: Congress and Treasury should seriously review information reporting rules and reduce the burden, especially on small businesses.
quote: Congress and the Treasury Department must undertake a serious review of the information reporting regime and reduce the burden on the public

title: Hold the IRS operating budget flat
proposal: The IRS operating budget should be held constant after inflation, with possible extra money only for IT modernization under strict conditions.
quote: The operating budget of the IRS should be held constant in real terms.

title: Close the IRS Office of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
proposal: The IRS Office of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion should be closed.
quote: The Office of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion should be closed.

title: Withdraw international tax information-sharing protocol
proposal: Treasury should withdraw from Senate consideration a protocol expanding the multilateral convention on sharing tax information among governments.
quote: The Treasury Department should withdraw from Senate consideration the Protocol Amending the Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters.

title: Oppose automatic exchange of financial account data
proposal: The administration should oppose the multilateral agreement on automatic exchange of financial account information.
quote: The new Administration should also oppose the multilateral Competent Authority Agreement on Automatic Exchange of Financial Account Information.

title: Withdraw from the World Bank and IMF
proposal: The U.S. should withdraw from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund and stop funding them.
quote: withdraw from both the World Bank and the IMF and terminate its financial

title: Give foreign aid directly, not through intermediaries
proposal: Any U.S. economic or humanitarian aid should be given directly by the U.S., not through international organizations, NGOs, or other nations.
quote: it should do so unilaterally—not through the pass-throughs of international aid

title: Balance the budget through spending cuts
proposal: Treasury should make balancing the budget a top goal, done by cutting spending while keeping strong defense and not raising taxes.
quote: The budget should be balanced by driving down federal spending while maintaining a strong national defense and not raising taxes.

title: Issue longer-term Treasury bonds
proposal: Treasury should issue longer-term bonds, and consider a 50-year bond, to lock in interest rates.
quote: issuing longer duration bonds, and even consider creating a 50-year treasury bill.

title: Send Americans an annual federal financial statement
proposal: Americans should get a yearly statement of federal revenues, spending, deficit, and debt, including their family's share of the debt.
quote: each year Americans should receive a financial statement of the U.S. government alerting citizens of the revenues,

title: Condition funding to international financial institutions on U.S. staffing
proposal: The U.S. should place more American professionals at international financial institutions and require this as a condition of future funding, while cutting or leaving institutions that work against U.S. interests.
quote: The U.S. must insist on the hiring and support of this human capital as a condition to future funding.

title: Adjust U.S. ownership stakes in international lenders
proposal: The U.S. should consider raising or lowering its ownership in international financial institutions to gain maximum leverage.
quote: The U.S. should also examine increasing or decreasing its ownership levels in these institutions in order to achieve maximum leverage.

title: Improve CFIUS mitigation monitoring
proposal: CFIUS should create a clearer, more transparent program for monitoring mitigation agreements and give national security agencies an equal voice.
quote: develop a more coherent—and transparent—mitigation monitoring program to complement the enforcement guidelines,

title: Publish a CFIUS penalty schedule
proposal: CFIUS should publish a schedule of penalties for violating its reporting and mitigation rules.
quote: CFIUS should publish a penalty schedule for violations of CFIUS reporting and mitigation requirements.

title: Make the Defense Department a CFIUS co-chair
proposal: Congress should make the Department of Defense a co-chair of CFIUS with Treasury.
quote: Congress should make the Department of Defense (DOD) a CFIUS co-chair with the Department of Treasury.

title: Require CFIUS review of Chinese greenfield investments
proposal: Congress should require CFIUS to review new U.S. facilities built by Chinese-controlled entities.
quote: Congress should close the loophole on greenfield investments and require CFIUS review of investments in U.S.-based greenfield assets by Chinese-controlled entities

title: Consider a school of financial warfare
proposal: Treasury should look at creating a school of financial warfare jointly with the Defense Department.
quote: Treasury should examine creating a school of financial warfare jointly with DOD.

title: Restrict and track U.S. investment in China
proposal: Treasury should closely evaluate U.S. investment in China, and the chapter calls for enhanced reporting and greater legal authority and restrictions.
quote: An enhanced reporting system is warranted, and greater legal authority and restrictions are appropriate.

title: Merge federal bank regulators
proposal: The administration should support legislation merging the OCC, FDIC, National Credit Union Administration, and the Federal Reserve's non-monetary supervision roles.
quote: supporting legislation to merge the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the National Credit Union Administration,
agency: Treasury / OCC / FDIC / NCUA / Fed / Congress

title: Create new low-regulation charters for financial firms
proposal: Policymakers should create new financial charters that remove activity limits and reduce rules in exchange for higher equity or risk-retention standards.
quote: Policymakers should create new charters for financial firms that eliminate

title: Repeal parts of the Dodd-Frank Act
proposal: Congress should repeal Titles I, II, and VIII of Dodd-Frank, which created the Financial Stability Oversight Council, orderly liquidation authority, and special utility designations.
quote: Congress should repeal Title I, Title II, and Title VIII of the Dodd–Frank Act.

title: End government control of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac
proposal: Treasury should work to end the conservatorships of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, wind them down in an orderly way, and move toward privatization, including privatizing the Common Securitization Platform.
quote: It should work to end the conservatorships and move toward privatization of these massive housing finance agencies.

title: Right-size FHA and Ginnie Mae
proposal: The missions of the Federal Housing Administration and Ginnie Mae should be reduced to fit a defined mission.
quote: The missions of the Federal Housing Administration and the Government National Mortgage Association (“Ginnie Mae“) must he right-sized to serve a defined mission.

title: Require FinCEN to publish annual anti-money-laundering data
proposal: Congress should require FinCEN to publish yearly data on suspicious activity and cash reports, prosecutions, convictions, fines, and private compliance costs.
quote: Congress must require FinCEN to annually publish data regarding:

title: Evaluate which anti-money-laundering rules work
proposal: Congress should require FinCEN and GAO to evaluate which parts of the anti-money-laundering system work, and require FinCEN to review its rules and report publicly.
quote: Congress should also require both FinCEN and the Government Accountability Office to undertake separate evaluations

title: Repeal the Corporate Transparency Act
proposal: Congress should repeal the Corporate Transparency Act, and FinCEN should withdraw its rule requiring small businesses to report their owners.
quote: Congress should repeal the Corporate Transparency Act, and FinCEN should withdraw its poorly written and overbroad beneficial ownership reporting rule.

title: Eliminate Treasury racial equity offices and committee
proposal: Treasury's Counselor for Racial Equity, Advisory Committee on Racial Equity, and Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility office should be eliminated.
quote: and created an office for Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility. All these should be eliminated.

title: Identify and interview Treasury staff in DEI programs
proposal: Every Treasury official who took part in DEI initiatives should be identified and interviewed to learn the scope of the programs and end them.
quote: Identify every Treasury official who participated in DEI initiatives and interview him or her

title: Publish Treasury DEI communications and training materials
proposal: All communications about Treasury's critical race theory and DEI work, and related training materials, should be made public.
quote: Make public immediately all communications relating to the work of the Treasury’s critical race theory and DEI initiatives.

title: Make DEI participation grounds for firing at Treasury
proposal: Taking part in critical race theory or DEI initiatives without objecting on constitutional or moral grounds should be treated as grounds for termination.
quote: Treat the participation in any critical race theory or DEI initiative, without objecting on constitutional or moral grounds, as per se grounds for termination of employment.

title: Eliminate Treasury's Climate Hub office
proposal: Treasury's Climate Hub office should be eliminated.
quote: The next Administration should eliminate the Climate Hub Office and withdraw from climate change agreements

title: Withdraw from the Paris Agreement and UN climate treaty
proposal: The U.S. should withdraw from the U.N. Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement.
quote: the next conservative Administration should withdraw the U.S. from the U.N. Framework Convention on Climate Change

title: Use Treasury tools to promote oil and gas investment
proposal: Treasury should use its tools and authority to promote investment in domestic energy, including oil and gas.
quote: The next Administration should use Treasury’s tools and authority to promote investment in domestic energy, including oil and gas.

title: End Treasury support for ESG investing efforts
proposal: Treasury should stop supporting international efforts that promote ESG investing and the Principles for Responsible Investment.
quote: It should reverse support for international public- (and private-) based efforts promoting Environmental, Social, and Governance

title: Consider moving Coast Guard and ATF back to Treasury
proposal: Congress should examine returning the Coast Guard from Homeland Security and ATF from Justice to Treasury.
quote: Congress should examine whether to return the Treasury’s former

title: Eliminate the U.S. Trade and Development Agency
proposal: Congress should eliminate the U.S. Trade and Development Agency, saying its work belongs to the private sector.
quote: Congress should eliminate the U.S. Trade and Development Agency (USTDA).
